`import { user as user }` and `const { id: id } = user` rename something to the name it already has. The short form means the same.

`--fix` removes the rename.

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad {"count": 3} */}
```js
import { load as load } from "./store.js";

const { id: id } = load();

export { id as id };
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```js
import { load } from "./store.js";
import { save as saveUser } from "./users.js";

const { id, name: userName } = load();

export { id, userName as name };
```

## Options

| Option | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ignoreImport` | `false` | Do not check imports. |
| `ignoreExport` | `false` | Do not check exports. |
| `ignoreDestructuring` | `false` | Do not check destructuring. |

{/* good {"options": [{"ignoreDestructuring": true}]} */}
```js
const { id: id } = user;
```
